ru.R: Кто-то сказал Иисусу: «Твоя мать и братья стоят на улице. Они хотят поговорить с {{deity_pronoun:тобой|Тобой}}.»

hi.L: और किसी ने उनसे कहा, "देखिए, आपकी माता और आपके भाई बाहर खड़े हैं और आपसे बात करना चाहते हैं।"
hi.B: किसी ने उन्हें बताया, "देखिए, आपकी माता और भाई बाहर खड़े हैं। वे आपसे बात करना चाहते हैं।"
hi.R: किसी ने यीशु से कहा, "आपकी माँ और भाई बाहर खड़े हैं। वे आपसे बात करना चाहते हैं।"

uk.L: І хтось сказав {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}}: «Ось {{deity_pronoun:твоя|Твоя}} мати й {{deity_pronoun:твої|Твої}} брати стоять надворі, шукаючи [нагоди] говорити з {{deity_pronoun:тобою|Тобою}}.»
uk.B: Хтось сказав {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}}: «Твоя мати й брати стоять там, надворі. Вони просять, щоб {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} з ними поговорив.»
uk.R: Хтось сказав Ісусові: «Твоя мати й брати стоять надворі. Вони хочуть поговорити з {{deity_pronoun:тобою|Тобою}}.»

ja.L: すると、ある人がイエスに言った。「ご覧ください。あなたのお母さまと兄弟の方々が、あなたと話そうとして、外に立っておられます。」
ja.B: ある人がイエスに知らせた。「ご覧ください。お母さまとご兄弟たちが外に立っておられます。あなたとお話ししたいとのことです。」
ja.R: ある人がイエスに言いました。「お母さまと兄弟の方たちが、外に立っていらっしゃいます。あなたと話をしたがっておられます。」

decisions.choice: the verse is present, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the verse is missing in some important early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts, among them the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, lack this verse. It may have been added to explain "the one telling him" in 12:48, or lost when a copyist's eye skipped from "to speak" at the end of 12:46 to the same words at the end of 12:47. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: look (L); look (B); not rendered (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: contigo, with no span
decisions.reason: "Contigo" is one word, "with you", and is written plain, as "conmigo" is; the other pronouns for Jesus (le, tu, tus) take the deity_pronoun setting as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Thầy" for "you" and "your", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As in Mark 3:32: someone in the crowd listening to him speaks to him as their teacher; "Thầy" is a noun of address that takes no setting.

decisions.choice: The speaker uses 합쇼체 and "선생님" for "you"; "서 계십니다" honours Jesus's mother
decisions.reason: Worded as the Korean Mark 3:32: Korean does not address a respected teacher as "you", so "선생님" stands for the pronoun and Literal does not bracket it.

decisions.choice: the speaker addresses Jesus politely ("ご覧ください", "お母さま", "立っておられます")
decisions.reason: Someone in the crowd speaks to a respected teacher and honours his family, as in Mark 3:32. "Behold" becomes "ご覧ください" (L, B); Readable leaves it out, as the English does.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν τῷ λέγοντι αὐτῷ· Τίς ἐστιν ἡ μήτηρ μου, καὶ τίνες εἰσὶν οἱ ἀδελφοί μου;

records.literal_gloss: He but answering said to the one telling him, Who is the mother of me, and who are the brothers of me?

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said to the one telling {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Who is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother, and who are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers?"
en.B: Jesus answered the one who had told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Who is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother? And who are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers?"
en.R: Jesus answered him, "Who is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother? Who are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers?"

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} (B, R); aquí están (L)
decisions.reason: Jesus says "look" to the crowd around him, so where Spanish uses a verb it is plural and takes the ustedes / vosotros setting. Literal says "aquí están", which points without addressing anyone, as the Greek word does.

decisions.choice: "제자들" at every level

decisions.choice: Vejam
decisions.reason: Jesus points to the people before him and speaks to those around him, so Portuguese uses a plural imperative addressed to them (vocês); "Vejam" is the usual word for showing someone something.

decisions.choice: doing the Father's will: what makes someone Jesus's family
decisions.reason: Those who do the will of the Father belong to Jesus's family (see 7:21).

decisions.choice: sister: women belong to this family too
decisions.reason: No sister was named at the door, but Jesus includes sisters among those who do God's will.

decisions.choice: to me
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the relationship at the end for a natural sentence.

decisions.choice: celui-là (L), with no gender span
decisions.reason: English Literal puts "that one / he" under the gender setting. In French "quiconque … celui-là" is ordinary generic wording that already includes everyone, so it takes no span (style guide §7); the list that follows names the sister too (m2).

"Ndugu" covers brothers and sisters alike, so it serves for Jesus's brothers in 12:46-49. Here the Greek names brother and sister side by side (meaning decision m2), so Swahili uses "kaka" (brother) to keep the two apart.

decisions.choice: yeye, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "he" as the traditional alternative to "that one". "Yeye" means he or she, so Swahili needs no span.

decisions.choice: "Cha Ta, Đấng ở trên các tầng trời" (L); "Cha Ta ở trên trời" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The form settled for the Vietnamese Matthew (as in 7:21).

decisions.choice: "người ấy", with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Người ấy" is already inclusive (style guide, section 7); the sentence goes on to name sister and mother.

decisions.choice: "하늘들에 계신 내 아버지" (L), "하늘에 계신 내 아버지" (B, R); "그 사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: As the Korean Matthew settles from 5:16. "누구든지" and "그 사람" already include men and women, so the English gender span has nothing to change, as in the Korean Mark 3:35.

decisions.choice: esse, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs a setting to choose between "that one" and "he". In Portuguese "esse" takes up "quem" as ordinary generic Portuguese, and the sentence goes on to name "irmã" and "mãe", so no setting is needed (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7).

decisions.choice: {{gender:ያ ሰው|እርሱ}} (that person | he) for the Greek emphatic "he"
decisions.reason: Amharic has the same two choices as English here: the masculine pronoun "እርሱ", as the Greek has it, or "ያ ሰው" (that person), which fits a sentence that goes on to name sister and mother. Balanced and Readable leave the pronoun out, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "御心" (L, B); "望まれること" (R)
decisions.reason: The Father's will is what he wants done (m1). "御心" is the living church word; Readable says it plainly, as Mark 3:35 does.
